questions.question:
n is a positive integer.
Column A: The count of perfect squares from 1 to n² (inclusive)
Column B: n
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: The perfect squares from 1 to n² are 1², 2², ..., n² — exactly n values. Column A = Column B = n.
questions.trap: Students include 0 as a perfect square (0²=0, but 0 is not in the range 1 to n² for n≥1).

questions.question: What is the minimum value of x² − 6x + 13?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: x²−6x+13=(x−3)²+4. Minimum at x=3: value = 4.
questions.trap: Students compute vertex x-coordinate correctly (x=3) but substitute back incorrectly: 9−6+13=16, or forget to add the constant after completing the square.

questions.question: A box has 3 red, 4 blue, and 5 green balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Given that the first ball is red, what is the probability the second is also red?
questions.explanation: After drawing one red ball, 11 balls remain: 2 red, 4 blue, 5 green. P(second red | first red) = 2/11.
questions.trap: Students compute P(both red) = (3/12)(2/11) = 1/22 instead of the conditional probability P(second red | first red) = 2/11.

questions.question: A rhombus has diagonals of length 10 and 24. What is the perimeter of the rhombus?
questions.explanation: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles. Half-diagonals: 5 and 12. Side = √(5²+12²) = √169 = 13. Perimeter = 4×13 = 52.
questions.trap: Students use perimeter = 2(d₁+d₂) = 2(10+24) = 68, treating diagonals as sides of a rectangle.

questions.question:
x is a positive integer with x² < 50.
Column A: Number of valid values of x
Column B: 7
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students include x=8 thinking √50≈8 (it≈7.07), or exclude x=7 thinking 7²=49 does not strictly satisfy x²<50.

questions.question: If x/2 + y/3 = 7 and x/4 − y/6 = 1, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Multiply first equation by 6: 3x+2y=42. Multiply second equation by 12: 3x−2y=12. Add: 6x=54 → x=9.
questions.trap: Students multiply both equations by LCM=12 and make coefficient errors, getting 6x+4y=84 and 3x−2y=12, then arithmetic errors when solving.

questions.question: Machine A produces 30 units per hour. Machine B produces 20 units per hour but breaks down for 15 minutes every hour. In 4 hours, how many total units do both machines produce?
questions.explanation: Machine A: 30×4 = 120 units. Machine B: active 45 min per hour = 3/4 of the time. Effective rate = 20×(3/4) = 15 units/hr. B in 4 hrs = 60 units. Total = 120+60 = 180.
questions.trap: Students compute B as 20×4=80 (ignoring downtime), getting total = 120+80 = 200 (option C).

questions.question: Monthly sales: Jan=200, Feb=240, Mar=180, Apr=300, May=260. Which month had the greatest percentage increase from the prior month?
questions.trap: Students pick February (absolute increase of 40 from 200 seems large) without computing April's 66.7% jump from 180 to 300.

questions.question: What is the distance between points P(1, −2) and Q(−3, 4)?
questions.explanation: Distance² = (−3−1)² + (4−(−2))² = (−4)² + 6² = 16+36 = 52. Enter 52 (the value under the square root).
questions.trap: Students compute the distance as √52 ≈ 7.21 and round to 7, or enter 7 instead of the radicand 52 as requested.

questions.question: If 4ˣ + 4⁻ˣ = 10, what is the value of 2ˣ + 2⁻ˣ?
questions.trap: Students take √10 = √(4ˣ+4⁻ˣ) and incorrectly conclude 2ˣ+2⁻ˣ = √10, missing the cross term +2 when squaring u.

questions.question: In how many ways can 8 people be divided into two unlabeled groups of 4?
questions.explanation: C(8,4) = 70 chooses 4 for one group. Since the groups are unlabeled (Group A = Group B), divide by 2: 70/2 = 35.
questions.trap: Students compute C(8,4) = 70 and stop (option B), forgetting to divide by 2 because the two groups are interchangeable.

questions.question:
a ≡ 3 (mod 7), b ≡ 5 (mod 7)
Column A: Remainder when a·b is divided by 7
Column B: Remainder when a+b is divided by 7
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: a·b ≡ 3×5 = 15 ≡ 1 (mod 7). a+b ≡ 3+5 = 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7). Both remainders are 1. Equal.
questions.trap: Students compute 15 mod 7 = 2 (arithmetic error: 15 = 2×7+1, so remainder is 1, not 2).

questions.question: $10,000 invested at 10% annual interest compounded annually. How many years until the account exceeds $13,000?
questions.trap: Students use simple interest: 10%/yr × 3 = 30%, so $10,000×1.3=$13,000 exactly (not exceeding). With compound interest, year 3 gives $13,310.

questions.question: In a circle, chord AB subtends a central angle of 70°. What angle does arc AB subtend at any point on the major arc?
questions.explanation: Inscribed angle theorem: inscribed angle = (1/2) × central angle. Inscribed angle = 70/2 = 35°.
questions.trap: Students confuse major arc (inscribed angle = 35°) with minor arc (inscribed angle on the other side = (360−70)/2 = 145°). The question specifies a point on the major arc.

questions.question: Which values of x satisfy (x − 1)/(x + 2) > 1? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: (x−1)/(x+2) > 1 → (x−1)/(x+2) − 1 > 0 → −3/(x+2) > 0 → x+2 < 0 → x < −2. Only x=−3 qualifies. B is excluded (division by zero).
questions.trap: Students cross-multiply without checking sign: x−1 > x+2 gives −1>2 (always false) or if they flip the inequality they get x < −2 but then include x=−2 (denominator=0, undefined).

options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students assume a symmetric distribution and guess Mean = Median. Perfect squares are right-skewed (large values like 81 and 100 pull the mean above the median).

questions.question: How many trailing zeros does 50! have?
questions.trap: Students compute only ⌊50/5⌋ = 10 (option A), missing that 25 = 5² contributes an extra factor of 5 for each multiple of 25 in 50! (namely 25 and 50).

questions.question: A circle passes through the origin and has center (3, 4). What is the equation of the circle?
questions.trap: Students write (x−3)²+(y−4)²=5 (option B), using r=5 instead of r²=25 in the circle equation.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 3 hours, Pipe B fills it in 4 hours, and Pipe C drains it in 12 hours. With all three pipes open, how many hours does it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.trap: Students add all three rates as filling: 1/3+1/4+1/12 = 8/12 = 2/3, giving time = 1.5 hours (forgetting C drains).

questions.question: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + c has roots 1, 2, and −3. What is the value of a?
questions.explanation: By Vieta's formulas: a = −(sum of roots) = −(1+2+(−3)) = −(0) = 0.
questions.trap: Students compute a = −(1+2+3) = −6 (option A), ignoring the negative sign on the root −3. The sum is 1+2−3=0, not 6.

questions.question: Which of the following equals (2³)⁴ ÷ 2⁵?
questions.trap: Students compute (2³)⁴ = 2³⁺⁴ = 2⁷ (adding instead of multiplying exponents when a power is raised to a power), then divide by 2⁵ to get 2².

questions.question: A fair die is rolled repeatedly until a 6 appears. What is the probability that exactly 3 rolls are needed?
questions.trap: Students compute (1/6)³ = 1/216 (probability of three 6s in a row), confusing the desired event (two non-6s followed by a 6).

questions.question: Which of the following numbers have exactly 3 positive divisors? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A number has exactly 3 divisors iff it is p² for a prime p. 4=2²→{1,2,4}✓. 9=3²→{1,3,9}✓. 25=5²→{1,5,25}✓. 16=2⁴→5 divisors✗. 36=2²×3²→9 divisors✗.
questions.trap: Students include 16 (also a perfect square), not realizing that only SQUARES OF PRIMES have exactly 3 divisors. 16=2⁴ has divisors 1,2,4,8,16 — five divisors.

questions.question: A frustum (truncated cone) has top radius 3, bottom radius 6, and height 4. What is its volume?
questions.trap: Students use V = πR²h = 144π (cylinder formula, option E) or V = π(R²+r²)h/3 = 60π, missing the cross-term Rr in the frustum formula.

questions.question: For an arithmetic sequence with first term 5, the 30th term equals 3 times the 10th term. What is the common difference?
questions.trap: Students mistakenly use a₂₀ = 3a₅ (misread the term numbers), getting 5+19d = 15+12d → 7d = 10, a non-integer answer.

questions.question: Which is the greatest: 2³⁰, 3²⁰, 5¹³, 6¹¹, or 10⁹?
questions.trap: Students compare by direct magnitude intuition. Base-10 logarithm comparison is the systematic approach: 3²⁰ ≈ 10^9.54, larger than 2³⁰ ≈ 10^9.03.

questions.question: How many integers from 1 to 200 (inclusive) are divisible by 3 or 5, but NOT by both?
questions.trap: Students compute 66+40−13=93 (the count divisible by 3 OR 5, including those divisible by both). The question asks for 3 XOR 5, excluding the 13 multiples of 15.

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 15. One number is removed, and the new average is 14. What was the removed number?
questions.trap: Students compute 15−14 = 1 (difference of averages) and report 1, confusing the change in average with the removed value.

questions.question:
x > 0
Column A: √(x+9) − √x
Column B: 3
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Let f(x)=√(x+9)−√x. At x=0, f=3. For x>0, f'(x)=1/(2√(x+9))−1/(2√x)<0 (since √x<√(x+9)). f is strictly decreasing, so f(x)<3 for all x>0. Column B > Column A.
questions.trap: Students test x=0 (f=3, equal) and choose C, ignoring that x>0 strictly. The function is strictly less than 3 for any positive x.

questions.question: In how many ways can 3 boys and 3 girls sit in a row such that no two boys are adjacent?
questions.explanation: Arrange 3 girls: 3! = 6 ways. This creates 4 gaps (B_G_G_G_B pattern). Place 3 boys in 3 of 4 gaps: P(4,3) = 4×3×2 = 24. Total = 6×24 = 144.
questions.trap: Students compute C(4,3) = 4 instead of P(4,3) = 24 for boy placement (order matters since boys are distinguishable), getting 6×4×6=144... actually getting 6×4×6 if they separately arrange boys: 6×4×3!=6×24=144. Common error: 3!×3!=36 (ignoring adjacency constraint).

questions.question: If the side of a square is increased by 20%, by what percentage does its area increase?
questions.explanation: New side = 1.2s. New area = (1.2s)² = 1.44s². Percentage increase = 44%.
questions.trap: Students double the percentage: 20%×2 = 40%, applying the linear scaling rule to an area (square) measurement.

questions.question: What is the sum of all integers from −50 to 50, inclusive?
questions.explanation: Every positive integer n pairs with −n to sum to 0. Plus the 0 term. Total sum = 0.
questions.trap: Students compute the sum from 1 to 50 as 1275 and double to get 2550, ignoring that negative integers cancel the positives.

questions.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = x² + 2x − 3. For what value(s) of x does f(x) = 0?
questions.trap: Students factor as (x−3)(x+1)=0 giving x=3 or x=−1 (option D), making a sign error: need two numbers multiplying to −3 and adding to +2, which are +3 and −1, so factors are (x+3)(x−1).

questions.question:
In a class of 30 students, 12 study French and 18 study Spanish. 6 study both.
Column A: Students who study neither language
Column B: 6
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: French∪Spanish = 12+18−6 = 24. Neither = 30−24 = 6. Column A = Column B = 6.
questions.trap: Students compute 12+18 = 30 = class size and conclude 0 study neither, ignoring the inclusion-exclusion principle.

questions.question: What is the units digit of 13⁴⁷ × 17²³?
questions.explanation: Units digit of 13^n cycles {3,9,7,1} with period 4. 47 mod 4 = 3 → units digit = 7. Units digit of 17^n cycles {7,9,3,1} with period 4. 23 mod 4 = 3 → units digit = 3. Product units digit: 7×3=21 → units digit = 1.
questions.trap: Students find the correct cycle position (3rd) but read the 3rd element as '3' instead of '7'. The cycle for units digit of 13^n is {3,9,7,1}: position 3 maps to 7.

questions.question: A and B together finish a job in 12 days. A alone takes 20 days. How many days does B alone take?
questions.trap: Students compute B = 20−12 = 8 or B = 12−20 = −8, subtracting days linearly instead of using rates (reciprocals of days).

questions.question: A circle has equation x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0. Which of the following are true? Select all that apply.
options: C. The origin lies outside the circle
D. The point (2, 2) lies on the circle
questions.trap: Students conclude the origin is outside (C). Plugging (0,0) into x²+y²−4x+6y−12 gives −12<0, which means INSIDE the circle (negative = inside for this equation form).

questions.question: The sum of interior angles of a convex polygon is 1620°. How many sides does it have?
questions.trap: Students solve n×180 = 1620 → n = 9 (option A), forgetting the −2 in the sum of interior angles formula.

questions.question: What is the sum of all positive factors of 48?
questions.trap: Students list factors and miss one: {1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,48}. A common miss is 16 (since 48/16=3). Correct sum = 124.

questions.question:
Events A and B: P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.5, P(A∩B)=0.3.
Column A: P(A|B)
Column B: P(B|A)
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students assume P(A|B) = P(B|A) (symmetry fallacy). Even if A and B are independent (0.6×0.5=0.30 = P(A∩B) ✓), P(A|B)=P(A)=0.6 ≠ P(B|A)=P(B)=0.5.

questions.question: In a right triangle, one leg is 3 more than the other and the hypotenuse is 15. What is the shorter leg?
questions.trap: Students set a²+(a+3)²=15 (forgetting to square the hypotenuse), getting 2a²+6a+9=15 → a²+3a−3=0, no integer solution.

questions.question: The sum of an infinite geometric series is 20 and the first term is 8. What is the common ratio?
questions.trap: Students write S = ar/(1−r) = 20 (starting sum from the second term), getting 8r/(1−r)=20 → r=20/28≈0.714.

questions.question: If xy = 12 and x + y = 7, then (x − y)² equals:
questions.trap: Students compute (x−y)² = (x+y)² − xy = 49−12 = 37 (option D), subtracting xy instead of 4xy.

questions.question: A right isosceles triangle has a hypotenuse of length 10. What is its area?
questions.trap: Students compute each leg as 10/2 = 5 (halving the hypotenuse instead of dividing by √2), getting area = (1/2)(5)(5) = 12.5.

questions.question:
n is a positive integer divisible by both 6 and 9.
Column A: Smallest possible value of n
Column B: 36
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: LCM(6,9) = 18 (since GCD(6,9)=3, LCM=6×9/3=18). Smallest n=18. Column A=18 < Column B=36.
questions.trap: Students compute 6×9=54 as the LCM (multiplying instead of dividing by GCD), choosing Column A=54 > Column B=36.

questions.question: What is the minimum value of f(x) = |x − 2| + |x + 1|?
questions.trap: Students evaluate f(0) = 2+1 = 3 and think x=0 is a special minimum point, not realizing the function equals 3 on the entire interval [−1, 2].

questions.question: The circumference of circle A is to the circumference of circle B as 2:3. What is the ratio of the area of A to the area of B?
questions.explanation: Circumference ratio = radius ratio = 2:3. Area ratio = (2)²:(3)² = 4:9.
questions.trap: Students use the circumference ratio 2:3 directly as the area ratio (option A), failing to square the linear ratio to get the area ratio.

questions.question: Evaluate C(10, 3) + C(10, 7).
questions.trap: Students compute C(10,7) by long division of 10!/7!3! making arithmetic errors, or forget the symmetry property C(n,k) = C(n,n−k).

questions.question: For what value(s) of k does kx² + 4x + k = 0 have exactly one real solution?
questions.explanation: Discriminant = 16 − 4k² = 0 → k² = 4 → k = ±2. Both values give exactly one real root.
questions.trap: Students solve 16−4k=0 → k=4 (treating k² as k in the discriminant formula b²−4ac where a=c=k).

questions.question:
A right circular cylinder has radius r and height h = 2r.
Column A: Volume of the cylinder
Column B: Total surface area of the cylinder
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: V = 2πr³. SA = 2πr² + 2πr(2r) = 6πr². V > SA when 2πr³ > 6πr² → r > 3. V < SA when r < 3. Cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Students substitute r=1: V=2π, SA=6π → B>A, concluding B is always greater. Must test other values (e.g., r=10: V=2000π, SA=600π, so A>B).

questions.question: What is the smallest positive integer that leaves remainders 4, 5, and 6 when divided by 5, 6, and 7 respectively?
questions.explanation: Remainders are each 1 less than the divisor: n ≡ −1 (mod 5), n ≡ −1 (mod 6), n ≡ −1 (mod 7). So n+1 is divisible by 5, 6, and 7. LCM(5,6,7)=210. n+1=210 → n=209.
questions.trap: Students compute LCM(5,6,7)=210 and report 210 (option C) as the answer, forgetting that n = LCM − 1 = 209.

questions.question: If log₃(x) = 4 and log₃(y) = 2, what is log₃(x²/y)?
questions.trap: Students compute 2×4/2 = 4 (dividing by log y instead of subtracting), or compute (log x)² − log y = 16−2=14.

questions.question: Which of the following infinite series converge? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A: Harmonic series — diverges (classic result). B: p-series with p=2>1 — converges to π²/6 ✓. C: Geometric series with |r|=1/2<1 — converges to 1 ✓. D: Terms oscillate between ±1, not → 0 — diverges. E: Terms → 1 ≠ 0 — diverges.
questions.trap: Students include A (the harmonic series). Since 1/n→0, students assume it converges. But the harmonic series diverges — this is one of the most important counterexamples in series theory.

questions.question: What is the sum of all positive two-digit multiples of 21?
questions.explanation: Two-digit multiples of 21: 21, 42, 63, 84 (next is 105, three digits). Sum = 21+42+63+84 = 210.
questions.trap: Students include 105 (three digits) or miss 84 (thinking 21×4=84 is below 100 but 21×5=105 is above), miscounting the terms.
